IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.summary: Mathlib supplies the two raw ingredients this roadmap builds on — Roby polynomial laws (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PolynomialLaw/Basic.lean`, definition, module structure and universe-polymorphic `toFun`/`isCompat` only) and the universal divided power algebra Γ_R(M) (`Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowerAlgebra/Init.lean`, with `dp`, `lift`, `map`) — plus Cayley–Hamilton for a single endomorphism (`LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly`), lifting of complete orthogonal idempotents along nilpotent kernels, t-structures and derived categories. Tau Ceti has a genuinely large Hecke-ring development (`TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/`, ~1100 declarations: abstract double-coset Hecke rings on top of Mathlib's `IsHeckeTriple`, associativity, commutativity, degree, GL_n coset decomposition, prime decomposition and Shimura's polynomial-ring presentation for n = 1, 2) and continuous group cohomology (`TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/`). What is genuinely missing is the entire determinant theory: no homogeneous degree-n polynomial laws, no multiplicative laws, no Chenevier determinants or pseudo-representations, no characteristic-polynomial ideal or Cayley–Hamilton quotient, no reconstruction theorem, and no Fitting ideals of modules at all (`Fitt₀` is absent from both libraries, so IHG.6's central bound cannot even be stated). The Hecke-on-complexes package (IHG.2), the spherical normalization and Hecke polynomial P_v(X) (IHG.3 — no Satake transform exists anywhere in either library), the interpolation (IHG.4) and the nilpotent descent schemas (IHG.5) are likewise absent; Tau Ceti's Hecke rings are classical GL_n(ℚ)/SL_n(ℤ) double-coset rings, not local spherical algebras with vol(K)=1.

targets.target: Polynomial laws natural in commutative coefficient algebras (Roby laws)
targets.note: Mathlib defines a polynomial law `M →ₚₗ[R] N` as a functorial family `S ⊗[R] M → S ⊗[R] N` for all R-algebras S (Roby 1963), with the universe-polymorphic extension `toFun`/`isCompat` and composition. Only `R` a CommSemiring is assumed, so this is at least as general as the layer's commutative coefficient algebras.

targets.target: Homogeneous polynomial laws of degree n and their degree decomposition
targets.note: `Mathlib/RingTheory/PolynomialLaw/` contains only `Basic.lean`; grepping it for `homogene`/`degree` finds nothing but the scalar-multiplication docstring, and no `IsHomogeneous`, coefficient or degree-n API for polynomial laws exists in either library. The file's own header says the coefficients of a polynomial law are left to 'further works'.

targets.target: Divided powers representing degree-n laws, with tensor and base-change maps
targets.note: Mathlib has the universal divided power algebra Γ_R(M) with `dp`, the weak universal property `lift`, functoriality `map`/`mapEquiv`, and divided power structures on ideals. Missing: the grading Γ^n, the representability theorem (degree-n homogeneous laws M → N ≅ Hom(Γ^n M, N)) and the base-change isomorphism S ⊗_R Γ_R(M) ≅ Γ_S(S ⊗ M) that the layer needs.

targets.target: Determinant: a multiplicative degree-n law D : A[G] → A with D(1)=1 (Chenevier determinant / pseudo-representation)
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'pseudorepresentation|pseudo-representation|pseudocharacter|pseudo-character|Chenevier'` over both Lean trees returns nothing, and no multiplicative-polynomial-law structure exists. Mathlib's `Matrix.det`/`LinearMap.det` are multiplicative maps on actual matrices/endomorphisms, not degree-n laws on a group algebra.

targets.target: Characteristic-polynomial identities for a determinant law
targets.note: Characteristic polynomials of matrices and of endomorphisms of finite free modules are in Mathlib, but the characteristic polynomial attached to a determinant law (D(X − g) expanded in the Λ^i coefficients) presupposes the determinant, which is absent.

targets.target: Direct sum/product, duality, scalar extension, restriction to subgroups and continuity criteria for determinants
targets.note: All of these are operations on determinant laws, which do not exist in either library; nothing analogous appears under `PolynomialLaw`.

targets.target: Agreement with the matrix determinant for a rank-n finite projective representation
targets.note: `LinearMap.det` is defined for endomorphisms of an arbitrary module (via a basis when one exists, 1 otherwise) and is multiplicative; but the comparison statement 'the determinant law of a rank-n finite projective representation is g ↦ det(ρ g)' cannot be stated without the determinant law.

targets.target: Trace comparison in the valid coefficient range (n! invertible)
targets.note: No trace/determinant reconstruction statement (Taylor's theorem that pseudo-characters and determinants agree when n! is invertible) exists in either library.

duplicates.note: R01.5 ('Recognition by Frobenius polynomials') explicitly consumes 'the arbitrary-degree multiplicative polynomial laws, Cayley–Hamilton algebras and representation theorem of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants', so it is a declared consumer rather than a competing owner; the overlap is only in the rank-two trace/determinant specialisation.

targets.target: Characteristic-polynomial ideal and Cayley–Hamilton quotient of an algebra with a determinant
targets.note: Mathlib proves Cayley–Hamilton for a single endomorphism of a finite free module (`aeval_self_charpoly`), which is the classical statement; Chenevier's CH(A,D) ideal generated by the values of the characteristic polynomial law, and the quotient algebra, are absent — grep for `CharpolyIdeal`, `CayleyHamilton` as an algebra structure returns nothing.

targets.target: Faithful determinant descent (a determinant descends to the CH quotient faithfully)
targets.note: Depends on determinants, which do not exist in either library.

targets.target: Generalized matrix algebra decomposition under residual multiplicity-freeness
targets.note: `grep -i 'GeneralizedMatrixAlgebra|generalized_matrix'` over declarations.tsv and both Lean trees finds nothing; Mathlib's `Matrix.fromBlocks` machinery is only the block-matrix calculus, not the GMA structure with its idempotents and bimodule entries.

targets.target: Reconstruction of a representation from a determinant over an algebraically closed field, up to semisimplification
targets.note: Nothing in either library reconstructs a representation from a determinant/pseudo-character; Mathlib's character theory (`Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Character.lean`) proves linear independence and equality-of-characters results over fields of characteristic zero only, not the degree-n determinant statement.

targets.target: Reconstruction over a complete local ring under residual absolute irreducibility
targets.note: Absent, for the same reason; there is no theory of residually absolutely irreducible lifts in either tree.

targets.target: Residual reducibility and lifting obstructions
targets.note: No reducibility-obstruction API exists.

targets.target: Reducibility ideals, extension modules and lattice constructions for congruences
targets.note: Reducibility ideals are absent. Mathlib has `Ext` in abelian categories, `groupCohomology`, and (new) continuous cohomology of a topological group in `Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/`, which Tau Ceti extends with restriction/inflation/corestriction, Shapiro and long exact sequences; so H¹ classifying extensions is available in general form. The arithmetic lattice and reducibility-ideal package is not.

duplicates.note: Declared consumer of exactly this layer's Cayley–Hamilton algebras and representation theorem; it adds Chebotarev density and coefficient descent rather than restating them.
AG2.3 lists IHG.1 among its dependencies and applies the reconstruction step; the overlap is in the use, not the construction.

R19.6 'Representations over Hecke algebras' constructs the determinant law from Hecke operators and proves representability under residual absolute irreducibility — the same reconstruction theorem, instantiated at a localised completed Hecke algebra.

L0 states that it imports 'congruence ideals/modules, generalized matrix algebras, pseudorepresentations, reducibility ideals and the general extension-class construction from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants' — i.e. exactly this layer's output — and adds only the automorphic period identification.

Pan's residually reducible theorem is formalised there 'including pseudodeformations, reducibility ideals, the global support argument'; the reducibility-ideal machinery is owned here and applied there.

targets.target: Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex and its finite image algebras
targets.note: Mathlib defines abstract Hecke rings of a Hecke pair/triple and Tau Ceti builds the ring structure, GL_n instance and coset calculus on top; but no action of a Hecke ring on a complex, and no notion of 'image algebra in End of a complex', appears in either library. The `line` for `IntegralHeckeRing` could not be pinned in declarations.tsv; the definition is in the cited file's final section.

targets.target: Perfect complexes over a commutative ring, bounded amplitude
targets.note: `grep -i 'PerfectComplex'` finds nothing in either tree. Mathlib has `HomologicalComplex`, `CochainComplex`, `DerivedCategory` and `CategoryTheory.Triangulated`, but no perfect-complex predicate.

targets.target: Comparison of chain, homotopy/derived and cohomology actions
targets.note: Mathlib has the derived category, the homotopy category and the homology functors, so the three targets of the comparison exist as categories; the statement comparing the three images of a fixed Hecke algebra is absent.

targets.target: Localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings; support and annihilator lemmas; finite generation
targets.note: Mathlib lifts complete orthogonal idempotents along a nilpotent-kernel surjection, which is the key ingredient for decomposing a finite algebra over a complete local ring into local factors; the decomposition statement for a semilocal complete algebra, and the associated support/annihilator lemmas for a Hecke action, are not formulated.

targets.target: Nilpotence bound for the ideal of degree-zero derived endomorphisms acting trivially on all cohomology of a bounded-amplitude object, via the t-structure filtration
targets.note: The t-structure machinery the proof needs (truncations, the standard t-structure on the derived category, its heart) is in Mathlib, but the nilpotence statement itself — that an endomorphism inducing zero on every cohomology object of an amplitude-[a,b] object has (b−a+1)-st power zero — is absent from both trees.

targets.target: Transport of the nilpotence bound to Hecke images, preserving the amplitude dependence
targets.note: Depends on the previous two targets; absent.

duplicates.note: TC.2 is the declared consumer of this layer's nilpotence bound for actual arithmetic complexes; it supplies the geometric comparison rather than reproving the abstract bound.

R19.6 asks for 'nilpotent structure and the distinction between reduced characteristic-zero specialisations and the whole integral Hecke algebra' — the same nilpotent-ideal phenomenon, but for the completed Hecke algebra of a fixed automorphic setting.

P7 owns perfect complexes over complete Noetherian local O-algebras, minimal representatives, Tor-amplitude, derived tensor and the amplitude distinctions this layer's nilpotence bound depends on; IHG.2 adds the Hecke action and the nilpotence theorem.
P9 relates amplitude, depth and component support for perfect complexes; it shares IHG.2's 'preserve the dependence on amplitude' obligation from the commutative-algebra side.

targets.target: The unramified local Hecke algebra of GL_n at v with T_{v,i} = char. function of K diag(ϖ^i,1^{n−i}) K and vol(K)=1
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `HeckeRing.GLn` builds exactly the classical global-integral analogues: the diagonal double cosets T(p,…,p,1,…,1) as `heckeGen k`, the p-local subring and Shimura's presentation. But this is the Hecke ring of the pair (SL_n(ℤ), integral matrices of positive determinant) inside GL_n(ℚ), built from finite double-coset counting; there is no local field, no hyperspecial K with a Haar measure normalised by vol(K)=1, and no p-adic group in either library.

targets.target: The Hecke polynomial P_v(X) = Σ (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} T_{v,i} X^{n−i} with T_{v,0}=1
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'hecke polynomial'` over both Lean trees returns nothing, and the q^{i(i−1)/2} coefficient pattern does not occur. Tau Ceti's `GLn/PolynomialRing` is a presentation of the Hecke ring as ℤ[X₁,…,X_n], a different object from this generating polynomial in X with Hecke coefficients.

targets.target: Normalized Satake transform and the isomorphism with the Weyl-invariant algebra
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'satake'` over `mathlib/Mathlib/` and `TauCeti/TauCeti/` returns zero hits; the layer's SR.4 prerequisite is itself unbuilt.

targets.target: Relation of P_v to the determinant character and Tate twist
targets.note: Requires both the Satake transform and the determinant of IHG.0; neither exists.

targets.target: Explicit conversion theorems between conventions (arithmetic/geometric Frobenius, inverse roots)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has arithmetic Frobenius at a prime of a number field (`NumberField.Chebotarev.isArithFrobAt` and the Artin symbol API under `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/`), but no dictionary relating Frobenius conventions to a Hecke polynomial.

targets.target: Verification at n=1 against class field theory and at n=2 against the classical modular-form Hecke polynomial
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the n = 1 and n = 2 cases of Shimura's Theorem 3.20 (surjectivity of ℤ[X₁,X₂] ↠ R_p) and has the GL₂ Hecke recurrence T(p^{k+1}) = T(p)T(p^k) − p·T(p^{k−1})·⟨p⟩-type relations, which is the classical n = 2 content the layer wants checked; Tau Ceti also has the Artin symbol of an unramified prime with its functoriality (`NumberField.artinSymbol`), the n = 1 class-field-theory side of the check. The check itself, against a Hecke polynomial that does not exist, cannot be stated. Tau Ceti's own file header records that general n needs two further unformalised steps.

duplicates.note: SR.4 owns the Satake transform and states it will 'provide the normalization dictionary consumed by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants'; the two layers share the normalisation conventions, with SR.4 the declared owner of Satake itself.

AG2.0 constructs 'the normalization dictionary among algebraic weights, geometric/arithmetic Frobenius, cyclotomic twists, normalized Satake and the integral Hecke polynomial of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3' — the same dictionary, cited to this layer.
TC.3 works with the same ambient Hecke polynomial and Levi Satake map for boundary induction, and factors it; it consumes rather than restates the normalisation.

targets.target: Compatible determinants over finite coefficient quotients from a dense family of classical Hecke systems
targets.note: Determinants do not exist in either library (see IHG.0), so no interpolation statement can be formulated.

targets.target: Uniqueness from Frobenius density via Chebotarev and continuity
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a substantial Chebotarev tree (Frobenius prime sets, the Artin symbol, tagged fixed fields, Galois-character orthogonality, von Mangoldt prime counting) but the density theorem is still under construction there, and in any case the uniqueness statement it would feed — that two continuous determinants agreeing on Frobenius elements coincide — presupposes determinants.

targets.target: Existence by polynomial-law identities on the completed group algebra
targets.note: `grep -i 'completedGroup|CompletedGroupAlgebra|iwasawaAlgebra|ProfiniteGroupAlgebra'` over declarations.tsv returns nothing: the completed group algebra O[[G]] of a profinite group is not in either library. The one nearby object is Mathlib's Amice transform, a linear equivalence D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧ between measures on ℤ_p and power series — the abelian G = ℤ_p case, and without a convolution ring structure. Polynomial-law identities on such an algebra are absent.

targets.target: Change-of-level, change-of-coefficients and passage to inverse limits for determinants
targets.note: Absent for the same reason. Mathlib's `Module.topologicalClosure`/inverse-limit machinery exists generically but is not applied here.

targets.target: Retention of the finite ramification set and continuity hypotheses
targets.note: No API for Galois representations/determinants unramified outside a finite set S exists in either library.

duplicates.note: R01.5 owns the Chebotarev recognition side of the same uniqueness statement (semisimple representations determined by characteristic polynomials at Frobenius), while IHG.4 owns the determinant-valued interpolation; they overlap on the density argument.
Constructs a determinant law from Hecke operators and Frobenius polynomials over a completed Hecke algebra — the concrete instance of this layer's abstract interpolation.
Declared consumer: it feeds an equivariant Igusa boundary Hecke polynomial into this interpolation.

targets.target: Theorem schemas taking a geometric Hecke comparison with a quantified nilpotent error ideal to a determinant in the appropriate quotient
targets.note: Neither the determinants (IHG.0) nor the nilpotent-ideal bounds (IHG.2) exist, so the schema has no components to combine.

targets.target: Functoriality and nilpotence bounds under products and extensions
targets.note: Mathlib has a complete general theory of nilpotent elements and nilpotent ideals with the usual closure properties, which is the ambient algebra; the specific nilpotence-index bookkeeping for Hecke error ideals under products and extensions is not present.

targets.target: Specialization to residual semisimple representations
targets.note: Semisimplification of a representation over a field is not in either library in the form needed (Mathlib has `Module.IsSemisimple` and Jordan–Hölder via `CompositionSeries`, but no residual semisimplification functor for Galois representations), and the determinant-valued statement is absent.

targets.target: Local conditions on extension classes and comparison of lattice choices for congruence applications
targets.note: Continuous group cohomology exists (Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology`, extended in `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/` with restriction, inflation, corestriction, Shapiro and the long exact sequence), so the extension classes have a home; but no local conditions on Galois extension classes and no lattice-comparison results exist.

duplicates.note: TC.2 builds the geometric Hecke comparison with its nilpotent error that this layer consumes as a hypothesis; the nilpotence bookkeeping is shared.

AutomorphicCongruences owns the congruence-module/Selmer-class side and the automorphic lower bounds; this layer's 'local conditions of extension classes and lattice choices' is the same material seen from the abstract side.

targets.target: Fitting ideals Fitt₀_T(M) of a finitely generated module and their functoriality
targets.note: Neither library has Fitting ideals: `grep -rn -i 'fitting ideal|fittingIdeal|Fitt_'` over both Lean trees returns nothing, and every `Fitting` hit in declarations.tsv is the Lie-theoretic Fitting decomposition (`LieModule.posFittingComp`). Since the central conclusion of both DKSW theorems is a Fitting-ideal containment, the layer cannot even be stated today.

targets.target: Rank-two continuous representation over the total quotient ring K of a complete reduced Noetherian local T, with characteristic polynomials in T[X]
targets.note: The ambient commutative algebra is present (total quotient rings via `IsLocalization` at non-zero-divisors, `IsLocalRing`, `IsNoetherianRing`, `IsAdicComplete`), and continuous cohomology of a topological group with topological coefficients is now in Mathlib and extended by Tau Ceti. What is missing is the representation-theoretic setup: continuous rank-two representations into GL₂ of a total quotient ring, their field-factor projections, and the characteristic-polynomial integrality hypothesis.

targets.target: Construction of the finite T-module M and the class in H¹(G, M(χ/ψ)) every cocycle of which generates M, with Fitt₀_T(M) ⊆ I
targets.note: Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology` (with Tau Ceti's restriction/inflation/Shapiro/long-exact-sequence layer on top) provides the H¹ in which the class would live — the roadmap assigns that API to ArithmeticGaloisDuality. The theorem itself, the generalised Ribet lemma of Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang Theorem 1.1 with residual indistinguishability allowed, is absent.

targets.target: The local-condition version for T ⊂ T̃ with the product bound (∏_{v∈P}(ξ_v(σ_v) − χ(σ_v)))·Fitt₀_T(N) ⊆ Ĩ
targets.note: DKSW Theorem 2.1; absent, and again not statable without Fitting ideals.

targets.target: Formal matrix ring with trace/determinant invariants and the integral matrix-invariant theorem
targets.note: Traces and determinants of matrices over a commutative ring are in Mathlib, but the invariant theory of the formal 2×2 matrix ring over ℤ (generation of the invariants of GL₂ acting on matrix tuples by traces and determinants, integrally) is not; `grep -i 'invariant theory|first fundamental theorem'` finds nothing relevant in either tree.

targets.target: Rational (algebraic-group) cohomology restriction and acyclicity statements
targets.note: Neither library has cohomology of representations of an affine algebraic group scheme (Hochschild/rational cohomology); Mathlib's `groupCohomology` is for abstract groups and Tau Ceti's `ContCohomology` for topological groups. Tau Ceti does have affine algebraic group schemes (`TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/`) and comodules, but not their cohomology.

targets.target: Koszul and Buchsbaum–Rim complexes with grade/regularity hypotheses and exactness
targets.note: Mathlib has regular sequences, their behaviour under flat base change and localisation, and a Rees-style depth characterisation via vanishing Ext. It has no Koszul complex (`grep -i 'koszul complex|KoszulComplex'` returns nothing; every `koszul` hit in Tau Ceti is the Koszul sign rule in graded/monoidal homological algebra) and no Buchsbaum–Rim complex.

duplicates.note: I.7 states it will 'import the general representation/lattice/extension-class/annihilator theorem from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.6, including this residual coincidence case', and verifies the Hilbert/Eisenstein hypotheses; the generalised Ribet lemma is stated in both but owned here.
I.6 builds the Ritter–Weiss modules and 'their Fitting-ideal functoriality' — the same missing Fitting-ideal API that this layer needs for Fitt₀_T(M) ⊆ I.
A readiness checkpoint aggregating I.6 and I.7, explicitly including 'the residually indistinguishable representation-theoretic proof'; it is bookkeeping over the same theorem.
ES.7 'Higher-rank derivatives and Fitting-ideal control' needs the same absent Fitting-ideal API, though for Kolyvagin systems rather than Ribet classes.

R03.3 develops regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules and complete-intersection criteria — the grade/regularity hypotheses this layer needs for the exactness of its Koszul and Buchsbaum–Rim complexes.

LocalGaloisDeformationRings.summary: Deformation theory of Galois representations is entirely absent from both libraries: `grep -i '\bdeformation'` over the 316811-line declarations index returns zero hits, and there is no Schlessinger criterion, no category of complete local Noetherian O-algebras as a deformation base, and no framed/unframed deformation functor. What does exist are ambient carriers this roadmap would build on: Mathlib's continuous representations of topological groups (`TopRep`, `Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/`) and continuous cohomology, `Module.Grassmannian` as a functor of rank-k quotients, `Algebra.FormallySmooth`/`FormallyUnramified`, `ringKrullDim`, `irreducibleComponents`, `IsAdicComplete`, and the very first pieces of p-adic Hodge theory (`BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` and Fontaine's θ in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/`, plus Witt-vector isocrystals). Tau Ceti adds Galois lattices with open kernels, adic-space foundations (valuation spectra and continuity) and normalized valuations on local fields. Genuinely missing: every object this roadmap names — framed local deformation rings, unramified/inertial-type/Steinberg/minimally-ramified conditions, Kisin's potentially semistable rings, Breuil–Kisin modules, bounded-height Frobenius-stable lattice moduli and local models, Fontaine–Laffaille conditions, ordinary flag schemes and determinant-ordinary quotients. No layer of this roadmap has any of its stated theorems in the libraries.

targets.target: Bounded-height Frobenius-stable lattice moduli inside projective Grassmannians
targets.note: Mathlib has the Grassmannian of rank-k quotients of a module as a functor on R-algebras with its base-change maps, which is the ambient space the layer works in. The Frobenius-stable lattice locus, the height bound and the moduli problem itself are absent; there is no Breuil–Kisin or φ-module theory in either library (`grep -i 'kisin|breuil'` over both Lean trees returns nothing).

targets.target: Height equations, representability, projectivity and the universal lattice
targets.note: Nothing of this kind exists. Mathlib has projective morphisms and `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, but no local-model construction.

targets.target: Map to the framed deformation ring and the precise image on the generic fibre
targets.note: Framed deformation rings do not exist in either library.

targets.target: Fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings for every rank n and finite K/Q_p
targets.note: Mathlib has just begun p-adic Hodge theory: B_dR⁺ and B_dR are defined (for the ring of integers of a perfectoid, following Scholze) but the file's own TODO list still asks for θ on B_dR⁺ and the DVR property. There is no D_st, no Hodge–Tate weights, no inertial type and no potentially semistable deformation ring.

targets.target: Characteristic-zero point criterion, reduced/flat quotient properties, Kisin dimension formula
targets.note: Krull dimension of a ring is available in general, but the specific dimension formula for a potentially semistable deformation ring (and the flat/reduced quotient constructions) is absent.

targets.target: Fontaine–Laffaille deformation conditions in the unramified small-weight range, with filtration ranks, tangent spaces and formal smoothness
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'fontaine-laffaille|fontaine laffaille'` over both trees returns nothing. Formal smoothness of algebras is in Mathlib as an ambient notion only.

targets.target: Ordinary deformation functors with a full invariant flag and specified graded characters; representability, dimension and component maps
targets.note: Absent; and see L8, which owns the distinction between this flag-bearing functor and the determinant-ordinary quotient.

targets.target: Semistable, Steinberg and minimally ramified analogues away from p for rank n, with the nilpotent monodromy operator
targets.note: No Weil–Deligne representations exist in either library (`grep -i 'WeilDeligne|WeilGroup'` over declarations.tsv is empty), so the monodromy operator N has no carrier.

duplicates.note: R09.1 owns the projective parameter spaces themselves — Grassmannians, flag schemes and 'the closedness of the equations defining invariant subbundles and Frobenius-stable lattices' — which this layer consumes; the Frobenius-stable-lattice equations are stated in both.
R07.4 owns Breuil–Kisin modules and the height bound from the Eisenstein polynomial, the input to this layer's bounded-height lattice moduli.

G7 treats local deformation conditions as representable subfunctors with a point criterion and consumes 'the precise local comparisons and component support input used in ACC+ §6.2' that this layer exports; the local conditions themselves are owned here.
R08.3 constructs Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings for rank two; L7 states the same construction for arbitrary rank n and arbitrary K/Q_p, and says so explicitly.

R07.3 owns Fontaine–Laffaille theory with its exact weight interval and full-faithfulness range, and says 'additional local arguments at weights p and p+1 are required in R08/R22'; L7's Fontaine–Laffaille deformation conditions are that application.

targets.target: The ordinary flag scheme over the framed deformation ring and the image ring of its proper pushforward
targets.note: Framed deformation rings do not exist; flag schemes over a base do not exist either (Mathlib has `Module.Grassmannian` but no relative flag scheme).

targets.target: The determinant-ordinary quotient cut out by (ρ(g₁)−χ₁(g₁))⋯(ρ(g_n)−χ_n(g_n))=0 and the full characteristic-polynomial identities
targets.note: Characteristic polynomials of matrices exist; the ideal generated by ordered products of (ρ(g)−χ(g)) over a universal deformation ring does not, because the universal ring does not.

targets.target: Universal character coefficient rings, including their chosen torsion components
targets.note: No universal deformation ring of a character exists; Mathlib does have `Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/` character theory for finite groups, which is unrelated.

targets.target: The comparison between the two ordinary conditions under the published hypotheses, at the integral/reduced/characteristic-zero level
targets.note: Absent; both sides of the comparison are missing.

duplicates.note: L7 constructs the ordinary deformation functor with a full invariant flag and 'separate[s] the flag-bearing functor from its image after forgetting the flag'; L8 is the same distinction stated as the comparison with the determinant-ordinary quotient.
R21.3 builds ordinary Galois and deformation families and needs the same ordinary local condition; it consumes this comparison rather than proving it.

targets.target: Framed local deformation functor and its representability
targets.note: Continuous representations of a topological group on a topological module are in Mathlib as `TopRep`, and complete local Noetherian rings are expressible; but the deformation functor on Artinian O-algebras, Schlessinger's criterion and the universal framed ring are all absent — `grep -i '\bdeformation'` over declarations.tsv returns zero hits in both libraries.

targets.target: Tangent and obstruction description via H¹ and H² of ad ρ̄
targets.note: Both discrete group cohomology and continuous cohomology of topological groups exist, with functoriality, restriction, inflation and long exact sequences (the last mostly in Tau Ceti). The adjoint representation ad ρ̄ of a Galois representation, and the identification of H¹(ad ρ̄) with the tangent space of a deformation functor, are absent.

targets.target: Effect of fixing the determinant and of forgetting a framing
targets.note: Absent for the same reason.

targets.target: Archimedean (real-place) deformation rings at p=2
targets.note: Mathlib has infinite places of a number field and complex conjugation, but no deformation theory of the order-two local Galois group at a real place.

targets.target: Relation of a local deformation ring over O to residue-field extension and to restriction of global universal representations
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: R03.2 owns the abstract Schlessinger criterion, framed representability, hulls versus prorepresenting objects and the obstruction algebra; R08.1 applies it to the local Galois functor.

R04.1 defines framed and unframed deformations, continuity and determinant-fixed variants for the global group; R08.1 is the same definition for a local group, and R04.1 explicitly restricts to the local one.
R04.2 proves existence of universal framed rings and the framed-versus-unframed power-series comparison; the framing/determinant bookkeeping is stated in both.

targets.target: Unramified deformation condition and its representability
targets.note: No local Galois deformation conditions of any kind exist. Tau Ceti has unramifiedness of a prime in a field extension (`NumberField.Chebotarev.isUnramifiedAt_of_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet`) but not of a representation.

targets.target: Fixed inertial type deformation condition
targets.note: Inertial types require the inertia subgroup of a local Galois group and its representations; neither library has the local Galois group of a p-adic field as a named object with its inertia filtration.

targets.target: Steinberg/special condition including the monodromy operator
targets.note: No Weil–Deligne representations and no monodromy operator N exist in either library.

targets.target: Minimally ramified deformation condition

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions.summary: This roadmap sits entirely above the automorphic/Galois frontier of both libraries. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has automorphic representations, Artin representations, Galois representations attached to modular forms, base change, automorphic induction, symmetric-power functoriality, trace formulas, endoscopy or Sato–Tate: `grep -rn -i 'automorphic'` over both Lean trees hits only bibliography lines citing Shimura's book and the unrelated 'automorphic set' of racks, and `grep -rn -i 'sato.tate|equidistribut|langlands|fundamental lemma'` returns nothing at all. What does exist is the classical GL₂/ℚ carrier the endpoints would be stated about: Mathlib's `ModularForm`/`CuspForm` with Eisenstein series, dimension formulas, q-expansions, Petersson inner products and modular L-functions, and Tau Ceti's larger development — Hecke operators via the slash action, eigenforms, newforms with strong multiplicity one and Atkin–Lehner theory, the Sturm bound, and Wiener–Ikehara Tauberian machinery that a Sato–Tate equidistribution argument would consume. Three of the six layers (ML.0, ML.4, ML.5) are registries that bind theorems to sources and owners rather than proving mathematics; the three mathematical layers (ML.1–ML.3) have none of their theorems in either library.

targets.note: Registry bookkeeping, not mathematics. The only objects the register could currently point at are Mathlib's modular forms and Dirichlet characters; automorphic representations, infinity types, local parameters and conductors of automorphic representations have no carrier in either library.

targets.note: No normalization dictionary of this kind exists; the corresponding Satake/Frobenius dictionary is owned by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0 and is itself unbuilt.

OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLif.summary: Nothing in this roadmap's Hida-theoretic or lifting chain exists in either library. There is no completed group ring O[[G]] (`grep -i 'iwasawaAlgebra|completedGroup|CompletedGroupAlgebra'` over declarations.tsv is empty; every `iwasawa` hit in Mathlib is the unrelated `IwasawaStructure` used for simplicity of PSL₂), no ordinary projector, no Hida family or control theorem, no Galois representation over a Hecke algebra, no deformation ring and hence no R=T statement. The one genuine hit is the algebraic core of the ordinary projector: Mathlib proves the Fitting decomposition of a module with respect to an endomorphism — `LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow` and `LinearMap.isCompl_iSup_ker_pow_iInf_range_pow` for Artinian and Noetherian modules — which is precisely the finite-module statement PadicFamilies L0a asks for, though the idempotent e = lim U^{n!} itself is not constructed. Around it sit the classical carriers: Tau Ceti's modular-forms tower (Hecke operators, eigenforms, newforms, strong multiplicity one, Atkin–Lehner, U_p at bad primes, Sturm bound) and Mathlib's `ModularForm`/`CuspForm` with q-expansions, plus `PowerSeries` for weight algebras. Genuinely missing: the ordinary tower and its projector on Hecke complexes, Hida control and finite flatness, the ordinary Galois/determinant family, the ordinary R=T theorem, and the Skinner–Wiles residually reducible results including the Berger–Li–Zhu crystalline-to-ordinary criterion.

targets.target: Completed group algebras / Iwasawa algebras O[[G]] (consumed from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1)
targets.note: The general inverse limit lim_{n,U} (R/Iⁿ)[G/U] is not constructed in either library. Mathlib does have the abelian prototype: measures on ℤ_p (`AbstractMeasure`, notation `D(ℤ_[p], R)`) with Dirac elements, pushforward and Fubini contractions, identified with ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧ by the Amice transform — but as a *linear* equivalence over the base ℤ_[p] only, with no convolution product proved and the general-base case listed as a TODO in the file. Augmentation, density of O[G] and the universal property for continuous actions are absent.

targets.target: Ordinary projectors and their finite-level comparison (consumed from PadicFamilies L0a)
targets.note: Mathlib proves the Fitting decomposition M = ker(fⁿ) ⊕ im(fⁿ) for a sufficiently large n and an endomorphism of a module that is both Artinian and Noetherian — exactly the finite-module statement the ordinary projector is built from, and in greater generality (any ring, any such module). What is missing is the projector itself: that U^{n!} is eventually constant with value an idempotent e, its U-equivariance and naturality, and the inverse limit of these projectors over a tower of finite discrete quotients.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has the U_p operator on classical modular forms at a bad prime (`heckeUNat`, `heckeUCuspNat`) together with its q-expansion characterisation, so the operator the projector is formed from exists in the GL₂/ℚ case. Hilbert and quaternionic Hecke complexes do not exist, and no complex carries a Hecke action in either library.

targets.note: Absent; there is no deformation problem and no ordinary image to preserve.

PA.2 also consumes PadicFamilies L0a's projector and proves the finite-quotient and continuity hypotheses for its own tower — the same hypothesis-checking obligation as R21.1, for a different family of complexes.

PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp.summary: The p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL₂(Q_p) has no part of itself in either library, and neither does the coefficient theory it rests on: there is no Robba ring, no (φ,Γ)-module, no Herr complex, no smooth or admissible or locally analytic representation of a p-adic group, and no block decomposition of such a category (`grep -rn -i 'robba|phi.gamma|locally analytic representation|smooth representation'` over both Lean trees returns nothing but unrelated differential-geometry hits). Two genuine ingredients do exist. First, Mathlib's p-adic distribution theory: `AbstractMeasure`/`D(ℤ_[p], R)` with Dirac measures, pushforward and Fubini-style contractions, the Mahler basis (`mahler`, `PadicInt.mahlerEquiv`), and the Amice transform `AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv : D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧` — the coefficient ring on which a (φ,Γ)-module over Q_p is built, though only as a linear equivalence (the ring/convolution structure and the general base are TODOs in the file). Second, Tau Ceti's projective covers and injective envelopes of modules (`TauCeti.IsProjectiveCover`, `TauCeti.IsInjectiveEnvelope`, with existence and minimal-presentation comparisons), the module-theoretic prototype of R30.5's projective envelopes. Everything the roadmap actually names — Colmez's functor, locally algebraic vectors, blocks, Breuil–Mézard multiplicities, and the Paškūnas / Hu–Tan / Tung theorems — is missing.

targets.target: Import the analytic Robba/annulus coefficient rings from PadicHodgeTheory P7:annulus-foundations
targets.note: An import obligation, and the imported object does not exist: `grep -rn -i 'robba'` over both Lean trees is empty, and there are no rings of convergent Laurent series on an annulus. Mathlib does have the closest available coefficient ring, ℤ_p⟦X⟧ identified with measures on ℤ_p by the Amice transform, but only as a linear equivalence over the base ℤ_[p] (the file lists the general-base and bounded-power-series theory as TODO).

targets.target: Import étale (φ,Γ)-modules, the Galois equivalence, overconvergence and the Herr comparison from PG.0–PG.3
targets.note: Absent from both libraries; no semilinear φ/Γ action on a coefficient ring, no étale module, and no Herr three-term complex. The nearest carrier is Mathlib's `WittVector.Isocrystal` (a φ-semilinear structure over the fraction field of Witt vectors), which is a different object.

targets.target: Fix the GL₂(Q_p) covariance convention and prove the normalization bridge with R16.3
targets.note: Convention-fixing plus a bridge theorem between the p-adic and classical normalizations; neither side exists, since there is no local Langlands correspondence for GL₂ in either library. Note that this target is a theorem to prove, not an import obligation, which is why the layer is graded 'not built' rather than 'process' even though its other two targets are imports.

duplicates.note: PG.0 is the declared sole owner of the cyclotomic coefficient rings and the commuting φ, Γ actions; R30.1 imports them and constructs no second carrier.
PG.2 owns Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence and the Robba realization that R30.1 imports.
P7:annulus-foundations owns the Robba analytic coefficient rings themselves; P7's own text repeats the 'no second Herr or Wach' ownership fence.
L2 '(phi,Gamma)-modules and Iwasawa cohomology' is another consumer of the same PG.0–PG.3 package.

targets.target: The category of smooth mod-p representations of GL₂(Q_p)
targets.note: Mathlib has continuous representations of a topological group on a topological module (`TopRep`), but no smoothness predicate (every vector has open stabiliser), no abelian-category structure for smooth representations, and no representation theory of GL₂ over a p-adic field. `grep -rn -i 'smooth representation|locally profinite'` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Admissible unitary Banach representations and their duals
targets.note: Nonarchimedean normed-space foundations exist (`IsUltrametricDist`, `NonarchimedeanAddGroup`, complete p-adic normed modules), but no unitary Banach representation, no admissibility condition and no Schikhof duality.

targets.target: Locally analytic representations
targets.note: Locally analytic functions on a p-adic group are not defined in either library; the only `locally analytic` hit is a docstring about polar parts in Tau Ceti's complex-analysis contour theory.

targets.target: Completed group-algebra actions on the duals
targets.note: Measures on ℤ_p with Dirac elements and pushforward exist and are the abelian prototype of a completed group algebra, but no convolution product is defined on them and there is no O[[K]] for a compact p-adic group K.

targets.note: Absent; the categories do not exist.

targets.target: The mod-p classification of smooth irreducible representations in every residual characteristic, including exceptional low-characteristic blocks
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti has extensive finite-group modular representation theory (Brauer characters, blocks of finite groups are not present either) but nothing for GL₂(Q_p).

duplicates.note: SR.0 owns the abelian category of smooth representations of a general p-adic group, with smooth vectors, invariants and admissibility; R30.2 needs that carrier and adds the mod-p classification and Banach/locally analytic layers.
L0 owns the Banach spaces of locally analytic functions, the inductive-limit topology and the dual distribution algebra that R30.2's locally analytic category is built on.
O0 'Weight spaces and locally analytic representations' constructs the same locally analytic representation theory for a different application.

targets.note: Absent; `grep -rn -i 'colmez'` over both Lean trees returns nothing, and neither the source nor the target category exists.

targets.target: Functoriality and exactness where valid

targets.note: Absent; central characters of representations of a p-adic group are not defined in either library.

targets.target: The prescribed irreducibility statements
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Shares the (φ,Γ)-module side of the construction, though it applies it to Iwasawa cohomology rather than to GL₂ representations.

targets.target: Locally algebraic vectors in a Banach representation
targets.note: Absent; neither Banach representations nor locally algebraic vectors are defined.

targets.target: Identification of the locally algebraic vectors attached to de Rham representations with distinct integral Hodge weights
targets.note: De Rham representations and Hodge–Tate weights are absent from both libraries; Mathlib's p-adic Hodge theory stops at B_dR⁺/B_dR.

targets.target: Comparison with classical smooth local Langlands and the algebraic weight
targets.note: Absent; there is no local Langlands correspondence of any kind in either library.

targets.target: Nonvanishing and density/closure assertions used in modularity lifting
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: R16.3 owns the classical GL₂ local Langlands correspondence that this layer compares against, and explicitly records that 'the p-adic Banach correspondence of R30 is different theory'.
R06.3 owns the potentially semistable Weil–Deligne parameter of a de Rham representation, the object on the Galois side of this comparison.

targets.target: Blocks of the category of smooth mod-p representations of GL₂(Q_p)
targets.note: No block decomposition of any representation category exists in either library; every `Block` hit in declarations.tsv is either `MulAction.IsBlock` (blocks of a permutation action) or unrelated probability/combinatorics.

targets.target: Projective envelopes in those blocks
targets.note: Tau Ceti has projective covers and injective envelopes of modules with uniqueness, existence and the minimal-presentation comparison — the module-theoretic prototype of what the layer needs. They are stated for `Module R M`, not for a smooth-representation category of a p-adic group, which does not exist.

targets.target: Endomorphism-ring comparison of the projective envelope with a local deformation or pseudodeformation ring
targets.note: Absent; deformation rings do not exist in either library (see the LocalGaloisDeformationRings entries in this same batch), nor do pseudodeformation rings.

targets.target: Support and multiplicity statements for the local Breuil–Mézard results
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'breuil'` over both Lean trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Separate treatment of absolutely irreducible, reducible and exceptional blocks, and the small-p distinction
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: R30.2 proves 'the finiteness and compactness results needed for projective envelopes and deformation-theoretic endomorphism rings' and the mod-p block classification; R30.5 constructs the envelopes and the comparison on top of them.
The local (pseudo)deformation ring that R30.5 compares its endomorphism ring against is owned there.

targets.note: The table itself is bookkeeping, but the layer states that 'the full exceptional-block proofs remain R30.5–R30.6 construction targets', so mathematical content remains here; none of it is in the libraries.

duplicates.note: R32.2 'accounts for the progression from Kisin/Emerton to Paškūnas, Hu–Tan and Tung' and applies exactly these local theorems, including the p=3 case; R30.6 owns their local statements.
R31.6 supplies the local–global compatibility statements for the same branches of R32 and audits their globalisation inputs; R30.6 fences its own results as purely local.
The layer itself says the exceptional-block proofs are shared R30.5–R30.6 construction targets.
